key_insight: DEFEAT enables gradient-based crystal design by jointly optimizing composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors, including searches for photovoltaic absorbers.
engineering_relevance: The approach could accelerate solar-cell absorber discovery by targeting useful band gaps while penalizing energetically unfavorable designs.
method: Extend a pretrained EquiformerV3 model to continuous species weights and site occupancies without fractional-data retraining.
Use property-model gradients and a learned energy penalty to optimize composition and structure together.
Validate candidate band gaps and stability with SCAN calculations and assess finite-temperature competition using learned potentials.
evidence_signal: SCAN calculations confirmed ten novel crystal structures with band gaps within 20% of a 1.34 eV target on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias propagates into designs unless corrected in the objective; target gaps and near-hull energies do not establish solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
